extracted.intended_audience: horror authors, publishers, and Horror Writers Association (HWA) members (prospective nominees and nominators)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing what works are eligible for the Bram Stoker Awards, the award categories, how works become nominees (member recommendations and juries), and how voting determines finalists and winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: awarded for 'superior achievement' not 'best of the year'
rubrics_metrics.description: To ameliorate the competitive nature of any award system, the Bram Stoker Awards are given "for superior achievement," not for "best of the year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framing is deliberate and influences judging philosophy; the rules are designed to make ties possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: first published in English during year of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Any work of Horror first published in the English language may be considered for an award during the year of its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to the work's first English-language publication date (the year it is published).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The thirteen Bram Stoker Award categories are: Novel, First Novel, Short Fiction, Long Fiction, Young Adult, Middle Grade (added in 2022), Fiction Collection, Poetry Collection, Anthology, Screenplay, Graphic Novel, Nonfiction, and Short Nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories have varied over the years to reflect the state of the publishing industry and the horror genre; a work is considered within the appropriate category for its form/format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination path: HWA membership recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: HWA membership at large recommends worthy works for consideration; a preliminary ballot for each category is compiled using a formula based on these recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member recommendations feed into a formula (not further specified here) that helps form the preliminary ballot for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination path: Category juries compile preliminary ballots
rubrics_metrics.description: A Jury for each category also compiles a preliminary ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category has a jury that independently assembles a preliminary ballot in addition to the membership-driven preliminary ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-round voting by Active members determines finalists and winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Two rounds of voting by our Active members then determine first the Final Ballot (all those appearing on the Final Ballot are “Bram Stoker Nominees”), and then the Bram Stoker Award Winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round one produces the Final Ballot (nominees); round two selects the Winners from those finalists. Voting is restricted to Active members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design allowing ties
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules are deliberately designed to make ties possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ties can occur and the awards system accommodates them rather than forcing a single 'best' winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation timing and announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are announced and the Bram Stoker Awards presented at a gala banquet, normally during the period between March and June.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are presented annually at a gala event (timing typically March–June).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifetime Achievement Award: criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Lifetime Achievement Awards are occasionally presented to individuals whose entire body of work has substantially influenced Horror.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This award recognizes overall, career-spanning influence on the horror genre rather than a single work; it is given only occasionally.
